title: Autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit economics by applying workload-driven defaults and automation for batching, KV-prefix caching and quantization profiles, and to surface unit-econ impact via tooling. This PR introduces an autotune pipeline that recommends and applies conservative defaults for common production workloads, a set of quantization profile artifacts for supported models, and a small unit-econ toolkit (CLI + backend endpoints) to estimate expected cost/latency impact before rollout. Changes: 1) autoscaler/autotune service: new autotune controller that analyzes recent request histograms, latency SLOs and model compatibility to compute batching and cache defaults; 2) runtime defaults: add a DefaultsRegistry that serves per-model and per-route suggestions for batch_size, max_wait_ms, cache_ttl, and kv_cache_enabled; 3) quant profiles: add quant_profiles/{model}-{profile}.yaml artifacts and loader in model-registry for runtime selection and fallback; 4) unit-econ tooling: backend endpoints (/optimize/uecon/simulate) and a small CLI (redwood-uecon) to simulate cost and latency given traffic shapes; 5) tests and docs: end-to-end integration tests, unit tests for warm-cache heuristics, and docs/console screen for new unit-econ reports. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-2184) - [x] backend controller implemented - [x] runtime integration + feature flag - [x] quant profile artifacts packaged - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs + console changes - [x] smoke rollout to staging Testing: initial CI run failed on a flaky cache warm-up unit test (CacheWarmupTest::handles_concurrent_warmup) — fixed by adding a deterministic time-mock and retry path. Integration tests run in staging with a synthetic traffic generator (10k rps for 30 minutes) verifying that autotune suggestions do not increase p99 latency beyond SLO. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.feature.autotune and optimize.ui.uecon flags; staged rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h with automated rollback if cost increases >10% without quality improvements. Notes: this PR is conservative — defaults are suggestions and require explicit apply for critical routes; quant profiles are non-breaking and require explicit opt-in per model. Related: ENG-2190, PM-402. Merge: squash-merged after approvals and CI green.

release_notes:
- Added autotune controller to recommend batching/caching defaults per workload; gated behind runtime.feature.autotune.
- Introduced quantization profile artifacts and runtime loader; teams can opt-in per-model.
- Unit-econ simulator (redwood-uecon) to estimate cost/latency impact before applying defaults.
- New metrics and console report for suggestion application and rollback visibility.
notes: Conservative rollout. Operators should monitor optimize.uecon.suggested_cost_delta and optimize.autotune.applied_count. For critical low-latency routes, keep autotune disabled until validated in staging.
